evidence: Plaut. Epid. 1.1.15: perpetuōn' valuistī? (Lewis & Short s.v. valeō)
Traupman 18: hello, how’ve you been?, salvē, valuistīne?
terms.comment: Latin asks in the perfect, “have you been well?”, and the answer repeats the verb: Valuī. Spoken, the question is clipped to valuistīn'.

phrases.latin: Valēn'? valuistīn'? — Valeō, et valuī rēctius.
phrases.english: Are you well? Have you been well? — I am, and I’ve been better.

sources: Lewis & Short: valeo
